name: DWO Extreme Championship
notes: The fed's own June 2002 Champions page lists the belt without a contender; the same page lists Lethal against the Heavyweight title and Lana Day against the Women's.
epitaph: The belt the fed sold on what it could do to a body: eight inches of glass table, a thirty foot cage, a pit of acid. Switchblade won it on 23 May 2002 and defended it with both men's hands taped and doused in glass. Luke Lawless is a former champion by that autumn, Chryste holds it in the spring of 2003, and Kuff McSlade takes it in the first week of July and keeps it a week later in the main event, barely. By the end of September it is on Sean Quinn and being put on the line beside a title Callisto Bane has just forced another man to vacate.

name: DWO Heavyweight Championship
notes: Billed the DWO Heavyweight Championship on the fed's own 2002 Champions page and by Primetime Central's own New Era results, and the DWO World Title in the fed's own show scripts from the autumn of 2002 onwards.
epitaph: The top of the fed, and the belt its own Champions page described as brutal to reach and worth beatings to keep. John Miro won it on 21 April 2002 and the record loses it almost at once: AJ Trinidad is champion by that June, Adam Stryker by the autumn, Jackson Rust by the end of October, and none of the three changes is dated anywhere held. Lexis Bane's shutdown emptied it, and a World Title tournament through December 2002 put it back on Kaiowas at the first Travesty of 2003. He lost it on 20 April 2003 at Primetime Central's own New Era supercard, to Donny Diamond, inside the DWO Asylum — the only change in the whole lineage the record dates to the day — and he had it back by 10 July, when the fed's own commentary calls him the DWO World Champion in the middle of losing a non-title match.

name: DWO Intercontinental Championship
notes: The fed's own Champions page spells the belt Intercontiental; its own show scripts spell it Intercontinental and call it the IC Title.
epitaph: Third belt down the line and, by its own page's account, no less wanted for it. Angelus won it on 25 March 2002, the earliest dated reign anywhere in the DWO's record. Chryste held it twice and was offered the chance to be a triple champion with it against Adam Stryker's World title; Noah White carries it into 2003; by that July the fed vacates it and books four men to fill it at the pay-per-view. It ends on Damian, and it ends by decree — Callisto Bane made him choose between the belt and a Heavyweight title shot on the fed's own Relentless of 25 September 2003, and he threw it down.

name: DWO Pride Championship
epitaph: A belt the record catches only at the end. The DWO ran a number one contender's match for it on 10 July 2003, and by 9 October Kaos had won that shot and Regin was the champion, sitting on commentary during the challenger's match with, the card warned, every reason to get involved.

name: DWO Rising Dominance Championship
notes: The last-ever claim is Angelus Sorrow's own LOW bio card (promotions/low/archive/angelus-sorrow-bio-card.html), not a DWO document; the DWO record itself never records the reign.
epitaph: A belt for the fed's own lower divisions, filled by bracket: the second set of brackets to name the last two competitors ran on Travesty of 11 April 2003. Carys held it that May. It is the one DWO title whose end the record actually names, and the naming comes from outside — a Lights Out Wrestling bio card of July 2004 lists its wrestler's other-federation honours and calls him the DWO Rising Dominance Champion, last ever.

name: DWO Tag Team Championship
epitaph: Gina Muniz and Angelus held it from 16 May 2002, and the fed ran a number one contendership tag elimination for it at Shock Syndrome that ended in a no contest. Draven won it at UnStAbLe that September and Callisto Bane counted it among UnHoly's holdings the same week. By the spring of 2003 it is on Chryste and Carys, taken off Tyrone Grace's side; by October it is on Damian and Roulette, defending against Hecate and Arsenic. Christmas Chaos held a segment about the belts' own concept sketches, and a promise that whoever the new champions were would defend them the following Travesty.

name: DWO Women's Championship
epitaph: The belt the fed insisted other federations looked down on and its own women did not. Kristi Kiss won it on 23 May 2002 and lost it three weeks later in a ladder match at Shock Syndrome that the fed's own results page could only score as "Winner by ?: Kristi Kiss.. Lana Day.. Jaslene Myst..." — Lana Day pinned Kristi Kiss for it, Jaslene Myst took it off Lana Day, and Kristi Kiss won it back without a pinfall. The fed's own newsdesk reported three women holding a claim to one belt and its officials stumped. Nothing held says how it was resolved.
